text: Skip bug: mutating `entries` while iterating skips the element after each removal, so consecutive disabled entries survive (e.g. `[{enabled: False}, {enabled: False}]` returns one disabled entry). Fix: `return [e for e in entries if e['enabled']]`.
Over 10 GB: doubling hourly means the file halves going back from 100 GB at midnight, so 21:00 (three halvings) puts it at 100/8 = 12.5 GB.
Average throughput is 40 files per minute, not 45. Equal file counts mean the slow half takes twice as long, so time-weighting pulls the average to the harmonic mean: 2/(1/60 + 1/30) = 40.

No bug: the `n=name` default argument binds each name at lambda creation, so the output is every name uppercased in order. Without that default (`lambda: name.upper()`) it would be the classic late-binding bug where all handlers return the last name.

Trailing-remainder bug: when `len(items)` is not a multiple of `size`, the leftover items are silently dropped (`chunks([1,2,3,4,5], 2)` returns `[[1,2],[3,4]]`, losing `5`). Also raises ZeroDivisionError on `size=0` rather than a clear error.

Correct behavior: .gitignore only excludes untracked files, and `build/output.log` is already tracked, so git keeps reporting its changes. Run `git rm --cached build/output.log` and commit to untrack it (file stays on disk; note it will be deleted from other clones on pull).

Not more likely than not: only ~17% chance it's genuinely flaky. A flag pool of ~595 tests (100 true flakes + 495 false positives from 5% of 9,900 healthy) means 100/595 ≈ 0.168 — false positives outnumber true flakes 5 to 1.

Caller sees None: the `return None` in the `finally` block swallows the in-flight IOError, since a return from `finally` discards any propagating exception. Same trap silently discards the parsed value on success too — `cleanup()` alone in `finally`, without the return, gives normal propagation.

No output-affecting bug: this is the standard interval-merge — sort by start, extend the last merged window with `max` when the next start falls inside it, so overlapping, touching, and fully-contained windows all merge correctly. Only behavior to note: it treats closed intervals, so `(1,3)` and `(3,5)` merge to `(1,5)` — change `<=` to `<` if touching windows should stay separate.

No termination — and worse, `check` returns success anyway: inside an `if` condition, `set -e` is suppressed for the whole function body, so the failed grep doesn't exit or stop the function, `echo checked` runs, and its exit 0 becomes the function's status. Deploy runs even when grep finds nothing; make grep's status the return value (`grep -q ready /var/run/status || return 1`) to fix it.
